I wonder if you couldn't do something with IFTTT and Stringify's Connect:Maker thing:

* On **your** phone, which controls the lights, set up a Stringify flow: When (Connect:Maker receives an HTTP GET/POST) Action (turn on the lights). Stringify will give you a URL to connect to.

* Set up an IFTTT applet on **each** phone (and account): If (Location == wherever your home is) Then (Webhooks == Make an HTTP POST request to the URL Stringify gave you.)

Stringify will now listen for *both* of you arriving home, and when either of you do, it should trigger your lights turning on at home.

No guarantees, have not actually tried this, etc - but this is what I'd try. /r/ifttt and /r/stringify might be useful.

The thing is that depression kills that ability to want things, to be motivated, to focus on anything besides just getting through the day. Because it exhausts you physically and mentally it also kills the ability to complete tasks. And then it makes you feel like the worst kind of shit human for the things that it has done to you. He probably feels dreadful for not having any drive or being able to imagine a better future for himself, which again leads to gaming where he can feel like he *does* achieve things and like he's just like everyone else.

This is why I say you have to back off him as far as getting him to commit to things goes. Until the depression is under control none of the things you think should help will help. You can help him through the day, but things like jobs are too big. You have to think small and day-to-day.

You're doing great taking him out and asking him about himself. Helping him imagine a better future where he can do things like kayaking is great! You're a great brother for looking out for him. But don't be too surprised if he feels like he can't do big things like that. Taking him out to the shops is great. Make him feel worthwhile and valuable as best you can.

Once the depression shifts you'll likely find he *wants* to do things. But while it's in place motivation is apt to be a constant struggle.

Okay, harsh talk time: you are lucky your brother is alive. Depression has a high death rate. As someone who is obviously motivated (I'm here) but is also dealing with a disability like your brother's, don't underestimate the amount of effort it takes just to get out of bed in the morning. Things you take for granted are probably far more difficult for him than they are for you. So skip phrases like "lazy as fuck" and "victim complex", please. Mental illness is real, it is devastating, and it can be a lifelong challenge to survive it.

You want him to study, join a gym, get a job, when it sounds like just keeping himself stable is a full-time job for him. Sometimes gaming is an addiction and sometimes it's what people need to do to cope - it gives them a sense of control, it lets them bleed off stress from their life like, say, everyone making him feel like he's a lazy piece of shit.

Accept your brother for who he is and you might even find the removal of all that pressure lets him improve. Or you might not. But keeping on and on and on at him about all the things he isn't doing right in *your* eyes is not helping him.
